findings.issue_text: [BUG] The new useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable function calls ctx.hasPermissionInMetadata(rulesPermissions.update, folder) but `ctx` is never imported or defined in useAbilities.ts — the diff rewrites the entire import block (lines 14–29) and adds no import for `ctx`. This is an unresolved identifier: TypeScript compilation of useAbilities.ts fails with 'Cannot find name ctx', so the whole alerting feature module graph (every component importing useAbilities, including AlertRuleMenu and RuleActionsButtons.V2) fails to build and CI is red. If it somehow compiled, the hook would throw a ReferenceError at render time.

[BUG] useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities calls useGrafanaRulesSilenceSupport() and useCanSilenceInFolder(rule?.folderUid), but neither hook is imported in the (fully rewritten) import block of useAbilities.ts nor defined anywhere in the shown file — the file only defines useCanSilence, which this new code stops using. Unresolved identifiers: the file fails to compile with 'Cannot find name useGrafanaRulesSilenceSupport' / 'Cannot find name useCanSilenceInFolder', blocking the build; the author either fabricated these hook names or assumed hooks from a different module without adding the imports.

[BUG] getCloudRule({ name: 'Cloud' }, { rulesSource: mimirDs }) passes a second argument that does not match getCloudRule's factory signature, which takes a single partial rule identifier (where the data source is expressed via ruleSourceName inside the first object), not a separate { rulesSource } options object — and it passes the DataSource object from mimirDataSource() rather than the data source name. The mock factory ignores the second argument, so the test's 'Cloud' rule is still built against the default cloud data source instead of the Mimir data source the test intends to target — the RBAC assertions exercise the wrong rules source — or TypeScript rejects the extra argument and the test file fails to compile.

[BUG] GrafanaGroupLoader silently drops both transitional rule states: the 'Creating' state (ruler rule with no prom rule yet) and the 'Deleting' state (prom-only rule whose ruler rule is gone) are removed along with matchRules(), with no replacement handling for the ruler→prom propagation window. When a user creates a Grafana-managed rule, it is invisible in the rule list until the Prometheus API propagates it (previously shown with a 'Creating' icon); when a user deletes a rule, the row now renders as a fully actionable normal rule sourced from the still-unpropagated prom data — the user is offered Edit/Delete/More menu actions on a rule that no longer exists in the ruler, and clicking Edit navigates to a nonexistent rule. The deleted tests ('should render rule with url and creating state when only ruler rule exists' and 'should render delete rule operation list item when only prom rule exists') removed the only verification of these acceptance criteria, so the drop is silent.

[BUG] useAllRulerRuleAbilities hardcodes isFederated = false with a TODO, deleting the previous isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) check that made federated rule groups immutable, so federated Mimir/Cortex rule groups lose their UI-level immutability protection. For any consumer of useAllRulerRuleAbilities (including useRulerRuleAbility, which AlertRuleMenu calls for datasource rules), a federated rule group is no longer marked immutableRule, so Delete/Pause/Duplicate/Update actions become 'supported' and their buttons/menu items render for users holding the corresponding permissions — previously these actions were hidden for federated groups. A user can now attempt destructive actions on federated rules that the old UI deliberately blocked.

[BUG] The new GrafanaRuleListItem drops the returnTo parameter from the rule href: the deleted GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx built createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo }) while the replacement builds createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`) with no returnTo. Users navigating from the (filtered) rule list into a rule's detail view lose the return-to context; the 'back to list' affordance on the rule page no longer returns them to the list state they came from (filters/scroll position), a regression against the deleted component's behavior that no test in the diff asserts either way.

[ADVISORY] The new menu verification test grants AlertingRuleDelete and folder-level delete permission but asserts exactly 4 menu items (silence, copy link, duplicate, export) and never asserts ui.menuItems.delete(), which is defined in the ui selector block but unused — so the Delete action's availability from the new prom-only list path is unverified by the diff's own tests. If Delete is intended to be reachable from the new list view (the PR's stated goal of restoring ruler-independent actions), its absence or presence is not pinned by any assertion: a regression that silently removes the Delete menu item, or an implementation that leaves it gated on the now-optional rulerRule, would pass this suite. Whoever relies on deleting Grafana-managed rules from the list view gets no guarantee either way.

[ADVISORY] Provisioned-rule detection in the list view migrates from the ruler payload (rulerRule.grafana_alert.provenance in the deleted GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx) to the Prometheus payload (Boolean(rule.provenance) and isProvisionedPromRule in useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities), making immutable-rule gating dependent on the prom rules API actually returning the provenance field. If the Grafana prom rules endpoint does not populate provenance (the deleted code's `?? is_paused` fallback pattern suggests the ruler payload was previously treated as the authoritative source for such metadata), provisioned Grafana-managed rules render as unprovisioned in the list: the Edit/Delete/Update actions that were previously suppressed for provisioned rules become available, and the provisioned badge disappears. The diff contains no test exercising a provisioned rule through the new prom-only path to pin this down.

[ADVISORY] The PR is titled 'Notification Rule Processing Engine' but the entire diff is a frontend alerting rule-list refactor (removing ruler API usage from the list view and re-plumbing RBAC ability hooks) — no line of this diff implements or relates to any notification processing engine. Reviewers and release-note/bisection tooling cannot trace any of this work to the stated intent; if the title reflects a real requirement, this PR contains zero implementation for it, and if the title is a mislabel the actual requirement ('remove ruler API requests from the list view') is nowhere stated, so the substantial behavior removals in this diff are reviewed against no requirement at all.

[BUG] Beyond removing ruler API requests, this diff deletes the 'Creating' and 'Deleting' rule-lifecycle rendering and the matchRules sync logic entirely, dropping a user-visible feature that the stated intent (removing ruler API requests from the list view) does not require removing. A just-created Grafana-managed rule (present only in the ruler) no longer appears in the list at all until the Prometheus-side sync catches up, and a just-deleted rule (present only in Prometheus) vanishes from the list instantly with no 'Deleting' in-progress indicator — previously both transitional states were rendered via RuleOperation.Creating/RuleOperation.Deleting, and matchRules plus its dedicated tests (deleted in GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx) enforced that the two sources stayed reconciled; users now get silent disappearance/appearance of rules with no consistency warning (the logWarning for prom-only drift was also deleted).

[BUG] useAllAlertRuleAbilities hardcodes isFederated = false with a TODO, removing the federated-rule-group immutability check that the previous implementation computed via isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group). Every remaining consumer of the deprecated-but-still-exported useAllAlertRuleAbilities now treats federated rule groups as editable, deletable, pausable and duplicatable — the UI renders Edit/Delete/Pause actions for federated groups that the backend will reject (or worse, that operate on the shared group), a silent behavior change hidden inside a hook-rename refactor.

[BUG] The new GrafanaRuleListItem builds the rule href as createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`) without the returnTo parameter that the deleted GrafanaRuleListItem in GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx included via createReturnTo(). Users navigating from the rule list to a rule's view page lose the 'return to list' navigation context that the old list items preserved, so back-navigation after inspecting a rule no longer returns them to their filtered list state.

[BUG] useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities gates AlertRuleAction.ModifyExport on isAlertingRule (prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule), whereas the equivalent ruler-based hook gated it on isGrafanaManagedAlertRule, which was also true for recording rules. Grafana-managed recording rules rendered from the prom-rule path lose the Export menu action even for users with AlertingRuleRead permission, since Grafana's rule export applies to recording rules as well as alerting rules.

[ADVISORY] useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities is a near-line-for-line copy of useAllRulerRuleAbilities (the code even carries a '// duplicate' self-diagnosis), a second hand-maintained ability table that already diverges from its twin in silence semantics, provisioned-rule detection (isProvisionedPromRule vs isProvisionedRule) and federated handling. The two ability tables will drift independently — and AlertRuleMenu now ORs abilities from both tables for the same rule, so any future divergence between them silently unions the permission results (an action granted by either table shows in the menu) rather than failing loudly; the next ability added to AlertRuleAction must be implemented in two places plus both hook wrappers.

[BUG] GrafanaGroupLoader now renders exclusively from the Prometheus rules API and deletes the ruler-reconciliation logic (matchRules, RuleOperation.Creating/Deleting), so the prom/ruler consistency window is no longer representable in the UI. A rule deleted from the ruler but still present in the Prometheus response now renders as a normal, fully actionable list item — Edit/Delete/Silence are offered for a rule that is mid-deletion (previously it showed the 'Deleting' state with no actions), so users can act on a rule that no longer exists and hit backend errors; conversely a just-created rule that exists only in the ruler disappears from the list entirely (previously shown as 'Creating') until Prometheus catches up.

[BUG] useAllAlertRuleAbilities previously enforced isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) to make federated rule groups immutable; the refactored version delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities where isFederated is hardcoded to false behind a TODO, dropping the invariant for every caller of the deprecated hook. Federated ruler rules (a Mimir/Cortex feature) that are not editable in the ruler now render Edit/Delete/Duplicate as supported-and-allowed in the UI wherever the deprecated hook is still used; every user of a federated group is offered actions that the backend will reject.

[BUG] useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities gates ModifyExport, Pause and Restore on prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) where the ruler-based version gated them on rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule), which also matched Grafana-managed recording rules. In views where only the prom rule is available (the new list view passes no ruler rule, so the ruler path contributes [false,false]), Grafana-managed recording rules lose the Export and Pause menu items that the old ruler-based check granted them; the action silently disappears for a legal rule type.

[BUG] The new GrafanaRuleListItem builds href via createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`) without the returnTo parameter that the deleted GrafanaRuleLoader included via createReturnTo(). Users navigating from the rule list into a rule view lose the 'back' return-to-list context that the old item component preserved, breaking the return navigation flow for every Grafana rule opened from the list.

[ADVISORY] Every ability is now computed as rulerAllowance OR grafanaAllowance across two independently implemented RBAC evaluators (ruler-path global/datasource permissions vs grafana-path folder-scoped hasPermissionInMetadata), making the effective UI permission the more permissive of the two paths whenever both rulerRule and promRule are present. Any future divergence between the two permission evaluations (e.g. one path gains a provisioning or availability check the other lacks) silently widens access instead of failing closed, and when the backend rejects an action the UI offered, the discrepancy is undiagnosable because no single path is authoritative; the same union pattern is duplicated in RuleActionsButtons.V2's canEditRule.

[ADVISORY] This diff creates a third parallel ability implementation — useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities plus a useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable explicitly commented 'duplicate' — alongside useAllAlertRuleAbilities and useAllRulerRuleAbilities, and the copies already disagree (Silence: useCanSilence(rule) vs silenceSupported && canSilenceInFolder && isAlertingRule; provisioned detection: isProvisionedRule vs isProvisionedPromRule; federated handling present vs hardcoded false). The next ability change must be applied in three places; any place missed produces rules whose action menu differs depending on which view (list vs details, ruler-backed vs prom-backed) rendered it — exactly the class of inconsistency this PR's union-based ORs are currently masking.

[ADVISORY] Provisioned detection for list items moved from the ruler rule's grafana_alert.provenance to the Prometheus rule's provenance field, and the two sources are not guaranteed to be populated identically. If the Prometheus rules endpoint omits provenance for provisioned rules, isProvisioned computes false and provisioned (immutable) rules render with Edit/Delete enabled in the list view; the user clicks through and the backend rejects, with no UI indication that the rule is managed.

[BUG] The PR's stated objective was only to stop calling the ruler API from the list view, but the implementation silently deleted the 'Creating' and 'Deleting' transition-state rendering (promOnlyRules/RuleOperation.Creating/RuleOperation.Deleting) along with matchRules, a user-visible feature drop that no accepted constraint covers — the 'Deleting' state in particular only ever needed prom data and did not require the ruler request at all. During ruler→prometheus propagation windows, rules mid-creation vanish from the list entirely (prom groups empty → nothing rendered, no placeholder) and rules mid-deletion now render as normal actionable rows (with Edit/Delete buttons via the new prom-based abilities) instead of showing a 'Deleting' marker — users can attempt to edit or re-delete a rule that is being removed. The deleted tests ('should render rule with url and creating state when only ruler rule exists', 'should render delete rule operation list item when only prom rule exists', the whole matchRules suite) were replaced rather than preserved, codifying the dropped behavior instead of surfacing it for acceptance.

[BUG] The stated intent is that promRule replaces rulerRule as the ability source ('we need to use promRule to check abilities'), but the implementation instead ORs two independently-computed permission checks with different internal logic (ruler path uses useCanSilence; prom path uses silenceSupported && canSilenceInFolder && isAlertingRule), so effective permissions everywhere this menu renders are now the union of two permission models rather than either one alone. Menu items appear that neither source alone would have granted: e.g. Silence renders when the folder-based prom check passes but the ruler-based useCanSilence check fails (or vice versa), and this union applies even in detail/rule-list contexts where rulerRule is fully present and the old single-source behavior was correct. Users see and can attempt actions the detail page (single-source) will then deny, and reviewers auditing permissions can no longer reason from one source of truth.

[BUG] useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities gates ModifyExport on isAlertingRule, whereas the old useAllRulerRuleAbilities gated it on isGrafanaManagedAlertRule (true for both alerting and recording rules), so Grafana-managed recording rules lose the Export menu item when only prom data is available. In the new list view (where rulerRule is no longer fetched, per the PR's own stated objective) users can no longer export Grafana recording rules from the rule menu, a capability regression that silently ships because the change is buried inside a hook described in its doc comment as merely 'designed to work with GrafanaPromRuleDTO'.

[ADVISORY] The @deprecated redirect of useAllAlertRuleAbilities onto useAllRulerRuleAbilities silently changes how rulesSourceName is derived — from getRulesSourceName(rule.namespace.rulesSource) to getGroupOriginName(groupIdentifier.fromCombinedRule(rule)) — a behavioral change to a still-exported public hook hidden inside what reads as a pure deprecation. Existing out-of-diff callers of useAllAlertRuleAbilities get their permission checks evaluated against the group-origin data source instead of the namespace's actual rulesSource; for any combined rule where these diverge (e.g. federated or remapped groups) abilities flip without those callers being touched or notified, and the deprecation comment gives no hint that behavior changed.

[ADVISORY] The rewritten GrafanaRuleListItem drops the returnTo parameter that the deleted GrafanaRuleLoader version passed to createRelativeUrl for the rule view link. Users clicking a rule from the new list view lose the 'return to' navigation context that previously brought them back to the filtered list view after viewing/editing a rule — a silent UX regression nobody accepted, introduced as an incidental side effect of the file rewrite rather than a deliberate decision.

[BUG] useAllRulerRuleAbilities hardcodes `const isFederated = false;` (replacing the previous `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` check in useAllAlertRuleAbilities), so federated rule groups are no longer treated as immutable. The `immutableRule` guard no longer covers federated rules, so Edit/Delete/Duplicate/Pause affordances are rendered for rules that originate from a federated (downstream) source and are not owned by the namespace they appear under; users are invited to mutate rules they do not manage, and the actions fail or hit the wrong source when invoked.

[BUG] useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined) — the path taken whenever skipToken is passed (rule absent or non-Grafana promRule) — fails open for Duplicate: loading is false when `!rule`, so `MaybeSupported` becomes AlwaysSupported and Duplicate resolves to [AlwaysSupported, global create permission] instead of failing closed. Combined with the OR in AlertRuleMenu (`canDuplicate = ruler || grafana`), a user with the global AlertingRuleCreate permission gets a Duplicate menu item for rules whose ruler-based ability marks duplicate as unsupported (e.g. rules from datasources where the ruler API is unavailable), producing an action that cannot succeed; every other ability in the undefined-rule path correctly fails closed, so Duplicate is a latent fail-open hole in the new hook's contract.

[ADVISORY] Within useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities the permission scoping is inconsistent: Update/Delete are checked folder-scoped via `ctx.hasPermissionInMetadata(rulesPermissions.update/delete, folder)` in useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable, but Duplicate's `rulesPermissions.create` (via toAbility) and ModifyExport's `exportAllowed` are evaluated as global permissions. A user with global AlertingRuleCreate or export permissions but no folder-scoped equivalents is shown Duplicate/Export menu items inside folders they cannot write to or export from; the buttons render on every such rule and fail server-side, teaching users that folder-scoped RBAC is unreliable and generating support noise for permission-denied actions.

[ADVISORY] Every action's can* value is now an OR of two independently computed ability systems (ruler-derived and folder-metadata-derived), e.g. `canPause = (pauseSupported && pauseAllowed) || (grafanaPauseSupported && grafanaPauseAllowed)`, creating two parallel hand-maintained permission pipelines that must stay in agreement. The OR is fail-open by construction: any future drift between the two ability tables (a permission added or scoped differently in one pipeline but not the other) silently widens which actions the UI offers, and the skipToken path already demonstrates such divergence (Duplicate); a single resolved ability per rule source would remove the places-to-update and the fail-open surface at once.

[BUG] The OR-composition of ruler and Grafana-prom abilities leaks 'supported=true' defaults from the skipToken path into non-Grafana rules, so the Duplicate menu item renders for cloud/Mimir rules the ruler path explicitly marked unsupported. For a cloud rule, useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities receives skipToken, which makes useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities run with rule=undefined: useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable returns loading:false, so MaybeSupported = AlwaysSupported, isPluginProvided=false, and Duplicate becomes [AlwaysSupported, getRulesPermissions('grafana').create]. A user with the Grafana-level create permission therefore sees canDuplicate = rulerDuplicate || true even when the ruler path returned [false,false] (e.g. ruler API unavailable or unsupported datasource), and clicking Duplicate on that cloud rule leads into a clone flow that cannot complete, reporting an error only after the user acts.

[BUG] ModifyExport support changed from 'any Grafana-managed rule' (rulerRuleType.grafana.rule) to isAlertingRule only, so the Export menu item silently disappears for Grafana recording rules rendered from the prom-rule path. In the list view (GrafanaRuleListItem / RuleActionsButtons.V2) only the prom path is evaluated, so a Grafana recording rule that previously offered ModifyExport (the old useAllRulerRuleAbilities used rulerRuleType.grafana.rule, true for recording rules) no longer shows Export; the capability is dropped with no error and no log, an unannounced feature regression for recording-rule users.

[ADVISORY] useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable swallows folder-fetch failures: when the folder query errors, folder stays undefined with loading:false and the hook returns isEditable/isRemovable false, indistinguishable from a missing folder. A transient failure of the folder permissions fetch makes edit/delete/pause buttons silently vanish for users who genuinely hold the permissions; the runtime error is never surfaced to the user or logged, so support sees 'I can no longer edit my rules' with no observable failure anywhere.

[ADVISORY] GrafanaGroupLoader now renders only prom-response rules, silently dropping both transient states the old matching logic surfaced: ruler-only rules ('Creating') and prom-only rules ('Deleting'), and deletes the matchRules logWarning that observed ruler/prom reconciliation mismatches. A user who just created a Grafana-managed rule sees nothing appear in the list until Prometheus propagation completes (previously a 'Creating' row), and a just-deleted rule vanishes instantly with no 'Deleting' indication; if ruler and prom ever disagree, the mismatch is now completely unobservable because the warning path was removed along with matchRules.

[ADVISORY] logWarning('Unable to construct an editable rule identifier') is called unconditionally in the render body of getEditableIdentifier, so when the identifier cannot be built it fires on every render of every affected row. On the polled rule list (~80 rows per page, RULE_LIST_POLL_INTERVAL_MS re-renders), any rule whose identifier cannot be constructed emits a warning analytics event per render per poll cycle rather than once per rule, flooding the analytics pipeline and burying the one signal that actually matters; the component also returns null so the user sees the actions disappear with no visible explanation.

goldens.comment: The rendered GrafanaRuleListItem is missing the required key prop for React list items. This can cause rendering issues when the list order changes.

RuleActionsButtons is invoked with only promRule, but SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer inside RuleActionsButtons still depends on a Grafana Ruler rule being present, so for Grafana rules coming from list views the 'Silence notifications' menu entry (now driven by Grafana Prom abilities) will toggle showSilenceDrawer without ever rendering the drawer. This means clicking 'Silence notifications' for these rules has no visible effect, even when abilities indicate silencing is allowed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff verifiably removes transitional-state handling in GrafanaGroupLoader: it drops the Ruler query (useGetGrafanaRulerGroupQuery), deletes matchRules(), and no longer renders the previous Creating (ruler-only) and Deleting (prom-only) list items (removed RuleOperationListItem block). It now renders only promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules as normal GrafanaRuleListItem rows, and the prior tests covering those states were removed. However, the finding’s claim that these mismatches *will* occur (propagation window leading to invisibility / actionable rows for deleted rules) is not provable from the diff alone; it’s an edge-case/behavioral-risk concern created by the change rather than a definitively demonstrated defect in the diff itself.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes federated-rule immutability logic from the abilities computation. Previously, `useAllAlertRuleAbilities(rule: CombinedRule)` computed `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` (note the removed import `isFederatedRuleGroup` and the old code reference). Now `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` just delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities(rule.rulerRule, groupIdentifierV2)`, and inside `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` the code explicitly sets `const isFederated = false; // TODO: Add support for federated rules`, meaning federated rule groups will no longer be treated as immutable (`immutableRule = isProvisioned || isFederated || isPluginProvided`). As a result, actions like Update/Delete/Pause/Duplicate can become supported/visible for federated groups when permissions allow, which is a behavior regression verifiable from the changed logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new GrafanaRuleListItem drops the returnTo parameter from the rule href: the deleted GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx built createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo }) while the replacement builds createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`) with no returnTo. adjudication.rationale: In the deleted `GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx`, the rule link href was built with `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo })` (using `createReturnTo()`), explicitly preserving list navigation context. The new replacement `GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx` now builds `href: createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`)` with no `returnTo` parameter, and this component is now used from `FilterView.tsx` and `GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx`. From the diff alone, this is a concrete behavior change that drops the prior return-to context and can regress the "back to list" behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new menu verification test grants AlertingRuleDelete and folder-level delete permission but asserts exactly 4 menu items (silence, copy link, duplicate, export) and never asserts ui.menuItems.delete(), which is defined in the ui selector block but unused — so the Delete action's availability from the new prom-only list path is unverified by the diff's own tests. If Delete is intended to be reachable from the new list view (the PR's stated goal of restoring ruler-independent actions), its absence or presence is not pinned by any assertion: a regression that silently removes the Delete menu item, or an implementation that leaves it gated on the now-optional rulerRule, would pass this suite. Whoever relies on deleting Grafana-managed rules from the list view gets no guarantee either way.

adjudication.rationale: In `GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx`, the new UI selector block defines `menuItems.delete`, and the `beforeEach` grants both global `AccessControlAction.AlertingRuleDelete` and folder-level delete permission via `setFolderAccessControl({ [AlertingRuleDelete]: true, ... })`. However, the menu test `should render correct menu actions when More button is clicked` only asserts silence/copy link/duplicate/export and then asserts `byRole('menuitem').getAll().length === 4`, never explicitly asserting the presence/absence of the Delete item. Given this PR also adds prom-rule-based ability checks in `AlertRuleMenu.tsx` (`canDelete` now ORs ruler + `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`), the delete path from the prom-only list view is a nontrivial behavior change that isn’t directly validated by a targeted assertion.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Provisioned-rule detection in the list view migrates from the ruler payload (rulerRule.grafana_alert.provenance in the deleted GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx) to the Prometheus payload (Boolean(rule.provenance) and isProvisionedPromRule in useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities), making immutable-rule gating dependent on the prom rules API actually returning the provenance field. If the Grafana prom rules endpoint does not populate provenance (the deleted code's `?? is_paused` fallback pattern suggests the ruler payload was previously treated as the authoritative source for such metadata), provisioned Grafana-managed rules render as unprovisioned in the list: the Edit/Delete/Update actions that were previously suppressed for provisioned rules become available, and the provisioned badge disappears. The diff contains no test exercising a provisioned rule through the new prom-only path to pin this down.

adjudication.rationale: Diff removes the ruler-backed list path (deleted GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx and GrafanaGroupLoader no longer queries getGrafanaRulerGroup) and switches provisioned detection to Prometheus rule data: GrafanaRuleListItem sets isProvisioned: Boolean(rule.provenance), useAbilities adds isProvisionedPromRule(promRule) = Boolean(promRule.provenance), and the DTO type adds optional provenance?: string. The finding’s core point is that immutability/provisioned gating now depends on the Prometheus API populating this new field, and there is no fallback to ruler metadata anymore. The diff does not prove the API will/waswo’t supply provenance, so it’s not a verifiable defect, but it is a concrete, diff-grounded risk plus a missing test case (no test covers a provisioned prom-only GrafanaPromRuleDTO ensuring Edit/Delete are suppressed and badge shown).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The PR is titled 'Notification Rule Processing Engine' but the entire diff is a frontend alerting rule-list refactor (removing ruler API usage from the list view and re-plumbing RBAC ability hooks) — no line of this diff implements or relates to any notification processing engine. Reviewers and release-note/bisection tooling cannot trace any of this work to the stated intent; if the title reflects a real requirement, this PR contains zero implementation for it, and if the title is a mislabel the actual requirement ('remove ruler API requests from the list view') is nowhere stated, so the substantial behavior removals in this diff are reviewed against no requirement at all.

adjudication.rationale: The finding hinges on the PR title and release-note/bisection traceability, which are not present in the diff and thus cannot be verified from it. Additionally, the claim that the actual requirement is “nowhere stated” is contradicted by new in-code comments explicitly stating the intent to “remove all requests to the ruler API in the list view” (e.g., AlertRuleMenu.tsx and RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx), and the diff clearly implements that by removing ruler API usage from GrafanaGroupLoader and prefetching in prometheusGroupsGenerator.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Beyond removing ruler API requests, this diff deletes the 'Creating' and 'Deleting' rule-lifecycle rendering and the matchRules sync logic entirely, dropping a user-visible feature that the stated intent (removing ruler API requests from the list view) does not require removing. A just-created Grafana-managed rule (present only in the ruler) no longer appears in the list at all until the Prometheus-side sync catches up, and a just-deleted rule (present only in Prometheus) vanishes from the list instantly with no 'Deleting' in-progress indicator — previously both transitional states were rendered via RuleOperation.Creating/RuleOperation.Deleting, and matchRules plus its dedicated tests (deleted in GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx) enforced that the two sources stayed reconciled; users now get silent disappearance/appearance of rules with no consistency warning (the logWarning for prom-only drift was also deleted).

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly removes the ruler-side query and reconciliation logic in `GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx` (deleted `useGetGrafanaRulerGroupQuery`, `matchRules`, and the `RuleOperation.Creating/Deleting` rendering, plus the `logWarning` on drift). The loader now renders only `promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules`, so any previously handled transitional/mismatch states would no longer be shown. However, the finding’s core claim that rules will actually exist “only in ruler” or “only in Prometheus” after create/delete cannot be verified from the diff alone (it depends on backend consistency guarantees). What *is* verifiable is a user-visible feature/UX regression and loss of drift warning if such mismatch occurs, making this a real diff-grounded concern but not a provable correctness defect from the patch itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] useAllAlertRuleAbilities hardcodes isFederated = false with a TODO, removing the federated-rule-group immutability check that the previous implementation computed via isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group). Every remaining consumer of the deprecated-but-still-exported useAllAlertRuleAbilities now treats federated rule groups as editable, deletable, pausable and duplicatable — the UI renders Edit/Delete/Pause actions for federated groups that the backend will reject (or worse, that operate on the shared group), a silent behavior change hidden inside a hook-rename refactor.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a behavior change: `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` (still exported, now marked deprecated) used to compute `isFederated` via `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` and include it in `immutableRule` gating edit/delete/etc. After the refactor it delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities(rule.rulerRule, groupIdentifierV2)`, and inside `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` the federated check is explicitly removed/disabled (`const isFederated = false; // TODO: Add support for federated rules`). This means federated-rule immutability is no longer enforced by these abilities, so UI ability results can incorrectly allow actions that were previously blocked.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new GrafanaRuleListItem builds the rule href as createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`) without the returnTo parameter that the deleted GrafanaRuleListItem in GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx included via createReturnTo(). Users navigating from the rule list to a rule's view page lose the 'return to list' navigation context that the old list items preserved, so back-navigation after inspecting a rule no longer returns them to their filtered list state.

adjudication.rationale: In the deleted GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx, GrafanaRuleListItem built the rule link as `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo })` with `returnTo` from `createReturnTo()`. In the new `GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx`, the href is `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`)` with no `returnTo` parameter. This diff objectively removes the returnTo context from list->view navigation, so any view-page/back navigation behavior depending on that parameter is regressed compared to the prior implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities gates AlertRuleAction.ModifyExport on isAlertingRule (prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule), whereas the equivalent ruler-based hook gated it on isGrafanaManagedAlertRule, which was also true for recording rules. Grafana-managed recording rules rendered from the prom-rule path lose the Export menu action even for users with AlertingRuleRead permission, since Grafana's rule export applies to recording rules as well as alerting rules.

adjudication.rationale: In `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, `AlertRuleAction.ModifyExport` is now supported only when `isAlertingRule` is true (`prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)`), i.e. only for alerting rules. Previously, the analogous ruler-based logic in `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` gated `ModifyExport` on `isGrafanaManagedAlertRule = rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)`, which would be true for Grafana-managed recording rules as well. With the new prom-rule path used by list items/menus, Grafana-managed recording rules would have `ModifyExport` unsupported and thus lose the Export menu action even if `exportAllowed` is true.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities is a near-line-for-line copy of useAllRulerRuleAbilities (the code even carries a '// duplicate' self-diagnosis), a second hand-maintained ability table that already diverges from its twin in silence semantics, provisioned-rule detection (isProvisionedPromRule vs isProvisionedRule) and federated handling. The two ability tables will drift independently — and AlertRuleMenu now ORs abilities from both tables for the same rule, so any future divergence between them silently unions the permission results (an action granted by either table shows in the menu) rather than failing loudly; the next ability added to AlertRuleAction must be implemented in two places plus both hook wrappers.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a second, parallel ability table in `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` that is explicitly marked `// duplicate` and largely mirrors `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, but with already-different logic (e.g. `isProvisionedPromRule` vs `isProvisionedRule`, different silence computation using `useGrafanaRulesSilenceSupport()`/`useCanSilenceInFolder`, and explicit `isFederated = false`). Separately, `AlertRuleMenu.tsx` now computes abilities from both sources and ORs them per action (e.g. `canDelete = (deleteSupported && deleteAllowed) || (grafanaDeleteSupported && grafanaDeleteAllowed)`), so any future divergence will silently widen permissions/UI availability rather than surfacing an inconsistency. This is a concrete maintainability/architecture risk created by the change, not a directly verifiable runtime defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] GrafanaGroupLoader now renders exclusively from the Prometheus rules API and deletes the ruler-reconciliation logic (matchRules, RuleOperation.Creating/Deleting), so the prom/ruler consistency window is no longer representable in the UI. A rule deleted from the ruler but still present in the Prometheus response now renders as a normal, fully actionable list item — Edit/Delete/Silence are offered for a rule that is mid-deletion (previously it showed the 'Deleting' state with no actions), so users can act on a rule that no longer exists and hit backend errors; conversely a just-created rule that exists only in the ruler disappears from the list entirely (previously shown as 'Creating') until Prometheus catches up.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly removes ruler-side loading/reconciliation in `GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx`: `useGetGrafanaRulerGroupQuery` is deleted, `matchRules` and `promOnlyRules`/`RuleOperationListItem` rendering are removed, and the component now renders only `promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules` as `GrafanaRuleListItem` (which always supplies `actions: <RuleActionsButtons promRule={rule} ... />`). This means the UI can no longer represent the prior explicit Creating/Deleting transitional states. However, the finding’s claim that such a prom↔ruler consistency window still occurs (and will therefore lead to users seeing actionable items for mid-deletion rules, or missing newly-created ruler-only rules) cannot be verified from the diff alone because it depends on backend consistency guarantees outside the PR; the PR may be assuming strong consistency.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] useAllAlertRuleAbilities previously enforced isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) to make federated rule groups immutable; the refactored version delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities where isFederated is hardcoded to false behind a TODO, dropping the invariant for every caller of the deprecated hook. Federated ruler rules (a Mimir/Cortex feature) that are not editable in the ruler now render Edit/Delete/Duplicate as supported-and-allowed in the UI wherever the deprecated hook is still used; every user of a federated group is offered actions that the backend will reject.

adjudication.rationale: In `useAbilities.ts`, the deprecated `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` no longer computes `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)`; it now derives `groupIdentifierV2` and delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities(rule.rulerRule, groupIdentifierV2)`. Inside `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, the federated check is explicitly removed and replaced with `const isFederated = false; // TODO: Add support for federated rules`, so federated rule groups will no longer be treated as immutable by this abilities computation. That directly drops the previous invariant that made federated rules non-editable/non-removable and can cause UI to show actions as available when they should not be for federated groups.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities gates ModifyExport, Pause and Restore on prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) where the ruler-based version gated them on rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule), which also matched Grafana-managed recording rules. In views where only the prom rule is available (the new list view passes no ruler rule, so the ruler path contributes [false,false]), Grafana-managed recording rules lose the Export and Pause menu items that the old ruler-based check granted them; the action silently disappears for a legal rule type.

adjudication.rationale: In `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` (new hook in `useAbilities.ts`), `ModifyExport`, `Pause`, and `Restore` are supported only when `isAlertingRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is true: `[AlertRuleAction.ModifyExport]: [isAlertingRule, exportAllowed]` and `[AlertRuleAction.Pause]/[Restore]: [MaybeSupportedUnlessImmutable && isAlertingRule, ...]`. Previously, the analogous ruler-based logic (`useAllRulerRuleAbilities`) gated these on `isGrafanaManagedAlertRule = rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)`, which would include Grafana-managed recording rules as well. In the new list path (`GrafanaRuleListItem` / `RuleActionsButtons.V2` / `AlertRuleMenu`) the code can rely on prom-rule abilities (ruler rule may be absent), so Grafana-managed recording rules will lose Export/Pause/Restore options purely due to this narrower `alertingRule` check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new GrafanaRuleListItem builds href via createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`) without the returnTo parameter that the deleted GrafanaRuleLoader included via createReturnTo(). Users navigating from the rule list into a rule view lose the 'back' return-to-list context that the old item component preserved, breaking the return navigation flow for every Grafana rule opened from the list.

adjudication.rationale: In the deleted GrafanaRuleLoader/GrafanaRuleListItem, the rule link was built as `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo })` where `returnTo` came from `createReturnTo()`. The new `GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx` builds `href: createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`)` with no `returnTo` query param. This is a concrete behavior change visible in the diff and plausibly removes preserved navigation context when opening a rule from the list.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Every ability is now computed as rulerAllowance OR grafanaAllowance across two independently implemented RBAC evaluators (ruler-path global/datasource permissions vs grafana-path folder-scoped hasPermissionInMetadata), making the effective UI permission the more permissive of the two paths whenever both rulerRule and promRule are present. Any future divergence between the two permission evaluations (e.g. one path gains a provisioning or availability check the other lacks) silently widens access instead of failing closed, and when the backend rejects an action the UI offered, the discrepancy is undiagnosable because no single path is authoritative; the same union pattern is duplicated in RuleActionsButtons.V2's canEditRule.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce the described “union” permission logic: in AlertRuleMenu, canPause/canDelete/canDuplicate/canSilence/canExport are computed as (rulerSupported && rulerAllowed) || (grafanaSupported && grafanaAllowed) after calling both useRulerRuleAbilities(...) and useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(...). Similarly, RuleActionsButtons.V2 computes canEditRule with the same OR pattern between useRulerRuleAbility(...) and useGrafanaPromRuleAbility(...). This is a real, diff-grounded architecture/consistency concern: when both a ruler-rule and prom-rule representation exist, the UI will allow an action if either evaluator allows it, making the effective UI permission the more permissive of the two implementations. However, whether this is a concrete defect/security bug cannot be proven from the diff alone (it may be intentional to support list-view without ruler API), so it’s best classified as a non-bug but important review issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] This diff creates a third parallel ability implementation — useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities plus a useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable explicitly commented 'duplicate' — alongside useAllAlertRuleAbilities and useAllRulerRuleAbilities, and the copies already disagree (Silence: useCanSilence(rule) vs silenceSupported && canSilenceInFolder && isAlertingRule; provisioned detection: isProvisionedRule vs isProvisionedPromRule; federated handling present vs hardcoded false). The next ability change must be applied in three places; any place missed produces rules whose action menu differs depending on which view (list vs details, ruler-backed vs prom-backed) rendered it — exactly the class of inconsistency this PR's union-based ORs are currently masking.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce a new parallel ability path for Grafana Prom rules: `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities()` plus a duplicated editability helper `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable()` (explicitly annotated `// duplicate`) in `useAbilities.ts`. This now exists alongside the existing ruler-based `useAllRulerRuleAbilities()` (and `useAllAlertRuleAbilities()` still exists, even if it now delegates). The two implementations already differ in how Silence is determined (`useCanSilence(rule)` vs `[silenceSupported, canSilenceInFolder && isAlertingRule]`) and provisioning detection (`isProvisionedRule` vs `isProvisionedPromRule`). Separately, UI code now ORs together abilities from ruler and prom (`AlertRuleMenu.tsx` and `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx`), which can mask mismatches between these implementations and lead to view-dependent action availability if they drift further. This is an architecture/consistency maintenance concern grounded in the diff, not a directly verifiable functional bug on its own.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Provisioned detection for list items moved from the ruler rule's grafana_alert.provenance to the Prometheus rule's provenance field, and the two sources are not guaranteed to be populated identically. If the Prometheus rules endpoint omits provenance for provisioned rules, isProvisioned computes false and provisioned (immutable) rules render with Edit/Delete enabled in the list view; the user clicks through and the backend rejects, with no UI indication that the rule is managed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes provisioned detection in list-view paths to rely on the Prometheus rule object’s optional `provenance?: string` (added in `GrafanaPromRuleDTOBase`, and used via `isProvisionedPromRule()` in `utils/rules.ts`, `GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx`, `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx`, and `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities()`), after removing ruler API usage in the list view (`GrafanaGroupLoader` no longer calls `getGrafanaRulerGroup`). If the Prometheus endpoint ever omits `provenance` for provisioned rules, immutability (`immutableRule`) would not be detected and the UI could incorrectly enable edit/delete. However, the diff does not prove the API actually omits provenance for provisioned rules, so this is a concrete consistency/contract risk introduced by the refactor rather than a verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The PR's stated objective was only to stop calling the ruler API from the list view, but the implementation silently deleted the 'Creating' and 'Deleting' transition-state rendering (promOnlyRules/RuleOperation.Creating/RuleOperation.Deleting) along with matchRules, a user-visible feature drop that no accepted constraint covers — the 'Deleting' state in particular only ever needed prom data and did not require the ruler request at all. During ruler→prometheus propagation windows, rules mid-creation vanish from the list entirely (prom groups empty → nothing rendered, no placeholder) and rules mid-deletion now render as normal actionable rows (with Edit/Delete buttons via the new prom-based abilities) instead of showing a 'Deleting' marker — users can attempt to edit or re-delete a rule that is being removed. The deleted tests ('should render rule with url and creating state when only ruler rule exists', 'should render delete rule operation list item when only prom rule exists', the whole matchRules suite) were replaced rather than preserved, codifying the dropped behavior instead of surfacing it for acceptance.

adjudication.rationale: The diff verifiably removes the transition-state rendering logic in the Grafana list view: `GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx` deletes the ruler-group query (`useGetGrafanaRulerGroupQuery`), deletes `matchRules`, and removes both the `RuleOperation.Creating` placeholder path and the `promOnlyRules` -> `RuleOperationListItem` (Deleting) rendering. It now renders only `promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules.map(...)`, so if the Prometheus response lacks a rule (or a group) there is no longer any fallback UI showing Creating/Deleting states. The prior tests covering these cases and the `matchRules` suite are also removed/replaced. However, the finding’s claim that propagation windows still occur and therefore users can act on “deleting” rules cannot be proven from the diff alone (the removed code even commented strong consistency), making this more of an unacknowledged behavior/scope change that needs justification/acceptance rather than a clearly provable defect from the patch itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The stated intent is that promRule replaces rulerRule as the ability source ('we need to use promRule to check abilities'), but the implementation instead ORs two independently-computed permission checks with different internal logic (ruler path uses useCanSilence; prom path uses silenceSupported && canSilenceInFolder && isAlertingRule), so effective permissions everywhere this menu renders are now the union of two permission models rather than either one alone. Menu items appear that neither source alone would have granted: e.g. Silence renders when the folder-based prom check passes but the ruler-based useCanSilence check fails (or vice versa), and this union applies even in detail/rule-list contexts where rulerRule is fully present and the old single-source behavior was correct. Users see and can attempt actions the detail page (single-source) will then deny, and reviewers auditing permissions can no longer reason from one source of truth.

adjudication.rationale: The diff verifiably changes the permission gating to a union of two independently-derived ability sources. In `AlertRuleMenu.tsx`, `canPause/canDelete/canDuplicate/canSilence/canExport` are now computed as `(rulerSupported && rulerAllowed) || (grafanaSupported && grafanaAllowed)` after calling both `useRulerRuleAbilities(...)` and `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(...)`. Similarly, `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx` computes `canEditRule` as an OR between `useRulerRuleAbility` and `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility`. The two models are not identical in this diff (e.g., Grafana prom silence uses `[silenceSupported, canSilenceInFolder && isAlertingRule]` in `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, while ruler uses `useCanSilence(rule)` inside `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`), so behavior can differ depending on which model grants. However, the finding overreaches by claiming menu items can appear when “neither source alone would have granted” (an OR cannot do that) and that the detail page remains single-source (the menu component itself is changed globally). This is still a concrete, diff-grounded consistency/authority concern rather than a conclusively provable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities gates ModifyExport on isAlertingRule, whereas the old useAllRulerRuleAbilities gated it on isGrafanaManagedAlertRule (true for both alerting and recording rules), so Grafana-managed recording rules lose the Export menu item when only prom data is available. In the new list view (where rulerRule is no longer fetched, per the PR's own stated objective) users can no longer export Grafana recording rules from the rule menu, a capability regression that silently ships because the change is buried inside a hook described in its doc comment as merely 'designed to work with GrafanaPromRuleDTO'.

adjudication.rationale: In `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, `ModifyExport` is now gated by `isAlertingRule` (`prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)`), meaning Grafana-managed *recording* rules will have `[supported=false, ...]` for export. Previously in `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, `ModifyExport` was gated by `isGrafanaManagedAlertRule = rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)`, which would be true for both Grafana alerting and recording rules. Since this PR removes ruler API usage in the list view and wires menus/buttons to Prometheus-based abilities (`useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` via `AlertRuleMenu`), recording rules can lose the Export menu item when only prom data is available, which is a behavior regression visible from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The @deprecated redirect of useAllAlertRuleAbilities onto useAllRulerRuleAbilities silently changes how rulesSourceName is derived — from getRulesSourceName(rule.namespace.rulesSource) to getGroupOriginName(groupIdentifier.fromCombinedRule(rule)) — a behavioral change to a still-exported public hook hidden inside what reads as a pure deprecation. Existing out-of-diff callers of useAllAlertRuleAbilities get their permission checks evaluated against the group-origin data source instead of the namespace's actual rulesSource; for any combined rule where these diverge (e.g. federated or remapped groups) abilities flip without those callers being touched or notified, and the deprecation comment gives no hint that behavior changed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` now derives `groupIdentifierV2` via `groupIdentifier.fromCombinedRule(rule)` and delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities(rule.rulerRule, groupIdentifierV2)`, which internally computes `rulesSourceName` using `getGroupOriginName(groupIdentifier)`. Previously, `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` computed `rulesSourceName` from `getRulesSourceName(rule.namespace.rulesSource)` and used that for `useIsRuleEditable(...)` and permissions. This is a real, diff-grounded behavioral change inside a still-exported hook marked only as deprecated, and it could change permission evaluation for existing callers without any call-site changes or explicit warning.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The rewritten GrafanaRuleListItem drops the returnTo parameter that the deleted GrafanaRuleLoader version passed to createRelativeUrl for the rule view link. Users clicking a rule from the new list view lose the 'return to' navigation context that previously brought them back to the filtered list view after viewing/editing a rule — a silent UX regression nobody accepted, introduced as an incidental side effect of the file rewrite rather than a deliberate decision.

adjudication.rationale: In the deleted `GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx`, `GrafanaRuleListItem` computed `const returnTo = createReturnTo();` and built the rule link as `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo })`, preserving navigation context. The new `rule-list/GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx` builds `href: createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`)` with no `returnTo` parameter, and `FilterView.tsx` now renders this new component directly. This diff-grounded change removes the previously present return-to context from rule links, which is a user-visible behavior regression.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] useAllRulerRuleAbilities hardcodes `const isFederated = false;` (replacing the previous `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` check in useAllAlertRuleAbilities), so federated rule groups are no longer treated as immutable. The `immutableRule` guard no longer covers federated rules, so Edit/Delete/Duplicate/Pause affordances are rendered for rules that originate from a federated (downstream) source and are not owned by the namespace they appear under; users are invited to mutate rules they do not manage, and the actions fail or hit the wrong source when invoked.

adjudication.rationale: In `useAbilities.ts`, `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` now sets `const isFederated = false;` (with a TODO) and no longer calls the previously-imported `isFederatedRuleGroup(...)` logic that existed in `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` (which had access to `rule.group`). Since `immutableRule` is computed as `isProvisioned || isFederated || isPluginProvided`, federated rules will no longer be considered immutable, so the ability map can mark Update/Delete/Duplicate/Pause/etc as supported/allowed when folder/permissions allow, causing UI affordances to appear for federated rules. This is a concrete behavior regression introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined) — the path taken whenever skipToken is passed (rule absent or non-Grafana promRule) — fails open for Duplicate: loading is false when `!rule`, so `MaybeSupported` becomes AlwaysSupported and Duplicate resolves to [AlwaysSupported, global create permission] instead of failing closed. Combined with the OR in AlertRuleMenu (`canDuplicate = ruler || grafana`), a user with the global AlertingRuleCreate permission gets a Duplicate menu item for rules whose ruler-based ability marks duplicate as unsupported (e.g. rules from datasources where the ruler API is unavailable), producing an action that cannot succeed; every other ability in the undefined-rule path correctly fails closed, so Duplicate is a latent fail-open hole in the new hook's contract.

adjudication.rationale: In `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, when `rule` is `undefined` (the `skipToken` path used by `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`), `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable` returns `{ loading: false }` for `!rule`, so `MaybeSupported` becomes `AlwaysSupported` (`const MaybeSupported = loading ? NotSupported : AlwaysSupported;`). That makes `duplicateSupported` resolve to `AlwaysSupported` (since `isPluginProvidedRule(rule)` will not mark it supported=false in this path), and thus `AlertRuleAction.Duplicate` can become supported/allowed based on global `rulesPermissions.create` even though no Grafana prom rule exists. Because `AlertRuleMenu` ORs ruler- and grafana-prom abilities (`canDuplicate = (ruler...) || (grafana...)`), this can surface a Duplicate menu item for non-Grafana/skipToken cases where the ruler ability is unsupported, yielding an action that cannot succeed. Other actions on the undefined path are effectively prevented by additional checks (e.g., `isAlertingRule`), but Duplicate is not.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Within useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities the permission scoping is inconsistent: Update/Delete are checked folder-scoped via `ctx.hasPermissionInMetadata(rulesPermissions.update/delete, folder)` in useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable, but Duplicate's `rulesPermissions.create` (via toAbility) and ModifyExport's `exportAllowed` are evaluated as global permissions. A user with global AlertingRuleCreate or export permissions but no folder-scoped equivalents is shown Duplicate/Export menu items inside folders they cannot write to or export from; the buttons render on every such rule and fail server-side, teaching users that folder-scoped RBAC is unreliable and generating support noise for permission-denied actions.

adjudication.rationale: In `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` the edit/delete allowance comes from `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable`, which explicitly checks folder-scoped permissions via `ctx.hasPermissionInMetadata(rulesPermissions.update/delete, folder)`. But `Duplicate` is allowed via `toAbility(duplicateSupported, rulesPermissions.create)` (no folder metadata check), and `ModifyExport` is allowed via `[isAlertingRule, exportAllowed]` where `exportAllowed` comes from `useAlertingAbility(AlertingAction.ExportGrafanaManagedRules)` (global). The tests also suggest folder-scoped create/read are relevant (`setFolderAccessControl` includes `AlertingRuleCreate`/`AlertingRuleRead`), so the diff-grounded behavior is that Duplicate/Export can be shown without corresponding folder-scoped permission checks, leading to UI offering actions likely to be rejected server-side for some users.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Every action's can* value is now an OR of two independently computed ability systems (ruler-derived and folder-metadata-derived), e.g. `canPause = (pauseSupported && pauseAllowed) || (grafanaPauseSupported && grafanaPauseAllowed)`, creating two parallel hand-maintained permission pipelines that must stay in agreement. The OR is fail-open by construction: any future drift between the two ability tables (a permission added or scoped differently in one pipeline but not the other) silently widens which actions the UI offers, and the skipToken path already demonstrates such divergence (Duplicate); a single resolved ability per rule source would remove the places-to-update and the fail-open surface at once.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces dual ability pipelines and then ORs them for each action (e.g. in AlertRuleMenu.tsx: `canDuplicate = (duplicateSupported && duplicateAllowed) || (grafanaDuplicateSupported && grafanaDuplicateAllowed)`). For non-Grafana rules it passes `skipToken` into `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, but `skipToken` is implemented as `undefined` and `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined)` still returns `Duplicate` as supported (`MaybeSupported` becomes `AlwaysSupported` when `loading` is false) and allowed based only on `getRulesPermissions('grafana').create` with no folder scoping. This means a non-Grafana rule (cloud/datasource) can incorrectly get `grafanaDuplicateSupported/grafanaDuplicateAllowed` true and thus surface Duplicate in the UI despite the grafana pipeline being intended to be skipped, i.e. a concrete fail-open behavior visible from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The OR-composition of ruler and Grafana-prom abilities leaks 'supported=true' defaults from the skipToken path into non-Grafana rules, so the Duplicate menu item renders for cloud/Mimir rules the ruler path explicitly marked unsupported. For a cloud rule, useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities receives skipToken, which makes useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities run with rule=undefined: useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable returns loading:false, so MaybeSupported = AlwaysSupported, isPluginProvided=false, and Duplicate becomes [AlwaysSupported, getRulesPermissions('grafana').create]. A user with the Grafana-level create permission therefore sees canDuplicate = rulerDuplicate || true even when the ruler path returned [false,false] (e.g. ruler API unavailable or unsupported datasource), and clicking Duplicate on that cloud rule leads into a clone flow that cannot complete, reporting an error only after the user acts.

adjudication.rationale: In `AlertRuleMenu.tsx`, the Grafana-prom ability path is OR-composed with the ruler path (e.g. `canDuplicate = (duplicateSupported && duplicateAllowed) || (grafanaDuplicateSupported && grafanaDuplicateAllowed)`). For non-Grafana rules it passes `skipToken` into `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(...)`. In `useAbilities.ts`, `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` converts `skipToken` to `undefined` and calls `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined)`, which sets `loading=false` via `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable` and then computes `MaybeSupported = AlwaysSupported` (since `loading` is false) and `duplicateSupported = AlwaysSupported`. It also uses `getRulesPermissions('grafana')`, so a user with Grafana create permission can get `[supported=true, allowed=true]` even though no Grafana rule is present. That makes `canDuplicate` true for cloud/Mimir rules even if the ruler ability is `[false,false]`, causing the Duplicate menu item to render incorrectly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] ModifyExport support changed from 'any Grafana-managed rule' (rulerRuleType.grafana.rule) to isAlertingRule only, so the Export menu item silently disappears for Grafana recording rules rendered from the prom-rule path. In the list view (GrafanaRuleListItem / RuleActionsButtons.V2) only the prom path is evaluated, so a Grafana recording rule that previously offered ModifyExport (the old useAllRulerRuleAbilities used rulerRuleType.grafana.rule, true for recording rules) no longer shows Export; the capability is dropped with no error and no log, an unannounced feature regression for recording-rule users.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new prom-rule-based ability path for Grafana rules (useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities / useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities) and in that new path sets ModifyExport support to `[isAlertingRule, exportAllowed]` where `isAlertingRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` (public/app/features/alerting/unified/hooks/useAbilities.ts). Previously, the analogous check in the ruler-rule path used `isGrafanaManagedAlertRule = rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)` and enabled ModifyExport for all Grafana-managed rules (including recording rules). The list view was refactored to render Grafana rules purely from the Prometheus/GrafanaPromRuleDTO path (GrafanaGroupLoader now only maps promResponse rules; GrafanaRuleListItem passes only `promRule` into RuleActionsButtons, and AlertRuleMenu now ORs ruler+prom abilities). As a result, Grafana recording rules displayed via the prom-rule path will no longer meet `isAlertingRule` and will lose the Export/ModifyExport menu item with no fallback in list view, which is a behavior regression introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable swallows folder-fetch failures: when the folder query errors, folder stays undefined with loading:false and the hook returns isEditable/isRemovable false, indistinguishable from a missing folder. A transient failure of the folder permissions fetch makes edit/delete/pause buttons silently vanish for users who genuinely hold the permissions; the runtime error is never surfaced to the user or logged, so support sees 'I can no longer edit my rules' with no observable failure anywhere.

adjudication.rationale: The new `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable` (in `useAbilities.ts`) only consumes `{ folder, loading }` from `useFolder(folderUID)` and then treats `!folder` as either “still loading” or “invalid folder UID”, returning `{isEditable:false,isRemovable:false}` with whatever `loading` is, and it never logs or exposes an error state. That does conflate “folder not found / not loaded” with any failure mode where `folder` is undefined, which can make edit/delete/pause actions silently disappear. However, the diff does not show `useFolder`’s error behavior (e.g., whether errors yield `loading:false` with `folder:undefined`), so the specific claim about transient query errors is not fully verifiable from this PR alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] GrafanaGroupLoader now renders only prom-response rules, silently dropping both transient states the old matching logic surfaced: ruler-only rules ('Creating') and prom-only rules ('Deleting'), and deletes the matchRules logWarning that observed ruler/prom reconciliation mismatches. A user who just created a Grafana-managed rule sees nothing appear in the list until Prometheus propagation completes (previously a 'Creating' row), and a just-deleted rule vanishes instantly with no 'Deleting' indication; if ruler and prom ever disagree, the mismatch is now completely unobservable because the warning path was removed along with matchRules.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly removes the dual-source reconciliation in `GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx`: it drops `useGetGrafanaRulerGroupQuery`, deletes `matchRules` (and its `logWarning`), and now renders only `promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules` (no more `RuleOperation.Creating` for ruler-only rules and no more `RuleOperationListItem` with `RuleOperation.Deleting` for prom-only rules). That is a real, diff-grounded change in UX/observability. However, whether this is a *bug* depends on runtime consistency/propagation guarantees between Ruler and Prometheus; the diff alone cannot prove that newly-created/deleted rules will be transiently missing, only that the code no longer attempts to represent those transients or warn about mismatches.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] logWarning('Unable to construct an editable rule identifier') is called unconditionally in the render body of getEditableIdentifier, so when the identifier cannot be built it fires on every render of every affected row. On the polled rule list (~80 rows per page, RULE_LIST_POLL_INTERVAL_MS re-renders), any rule whose identifier cannot be constructed emits a warning analytics event per render per poll cycle rather than once per rule, flooding the analytics pipeline and burying the one signal that actually matters; the component also returns null so the user sees the actions disappear with no visible explanation.

adjudication.rationale: In RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx, getEditableIdentifier() is called during render to derive `identifier` (const identifier = getEditableIdentifier(...); then if (!identifier) return null). In getEditableIdentifier(), when neither a `rule` is provided nor `promRule` passes `prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule)`, it executes `logWarning('Unable to construct an editable rule identifier');` and returns undefined. Because this happens in the render path, any row/component in that state would emit the warning on every render/re-render (and the list is polled/re-rendered frequently). The diff shows no throttling/memoization to ensure it fires once per rule, and the UI silently returns null (actions disappear). This is a concrete diff-grounded concern about excessive warning/analytics noise and poor UX, not strictly a functional correctness defect.
